narrative.overview:
A technical document is a line you travel. The outline is drawn as a vertical transit line with stations; the reader always knows which station they are at and how far along the line they have come. Every surface borrows from Swiss railway wayfinding: a cool near-white platform, deep blue-black ink, and a single signal vermilion that carries the line, the current station, focus, and progress. Nothing else is allowed to shout.

The chrome is quiet and dense (a 40px title bar, a 30px status bar, 12–13px UI text) so the reading column can be calm and generous: 16px Be Vietnam Pro at a 1.72 line height on a ~72ch measure. Tables are set like timetables, diagrams open like maps on a dotted ground, and code sits in tinted, hairline-bordered cases. Light and dark are both first-class and share every token name; dark mode lifts the vermilion and cools the ground rather than inverting.

Rejected explicitly: the generic gray IDE sidebar with a flat link list, and the earlier MarkText look.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (signal vermilion) used for line, station, focus, selection, progress, and the primary-button hover; everything else is ink on cool neutrals.
Outline rendered as a line diagram: a 3px track, ring stations sized by heading depth, segments filling as the reader passes them.
Section headings (h2) carry the same station ring on a hairline rule, tying the column to the outline.
Timetable tables: heavy ink head rule, hairline rows, no vertical rules, tabular figures.
Status bar's top edge is the reading-progress line.
Flat by default; one soft shadow reserved for floating layers.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion means "you are here / this is the line / this has focus". It is never used for decoration, headings text, or links.

rules.name: The Two Signals, Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Vermilion belongs to the route; Route Blue belongs to prose links. They do not swap.

rules.name: The Same Names in the Dark Rule
rules.body: Every color token exists under the same name in both `html[data-theme]` blocks; components reference tokens only, never a theme-specific literal.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Be Vietnam Pro sets every word that is not code, including headings, chrome, and Mermaid labels (15px). No second display face.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader compares (status counts, zoom %, word count, find count, table cells, ordered-list markers) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it sits in the document flow, it has no shadow. Only overlays and the selected segment get one.

dos: **Do** route every color through the theme tokens so light and dark stay in lockstep.
**Do** reserve signal vermilion for line, station, focus, selection, and progress (The One Signal Rule).
**Do** draw new navigational structure as stations on a line: hollow rings on a 3px track, sized by importance.
**Do** set tables as timetables: 2px ink head rule, hairline rows, no verticals, tabular figures.
**Do** keep chrome at 12–13px and the reading body at 16px × zoom on a 46rem measure.
**Do** use the floating shadow only for layers that sit above the document.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; all animation and transition is disabled under it.
donts: **Don't** fall back to a gray IDE sidebar with a flat link list for the outline.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue in chrome, or use Route Blue anywhere but prose links.
**Don't** add a second display face; Be Vietnam Pro sets every non-code word.
**Don't** put a logo in the title bar.
**Don't** give in-flow blocks (code, diagrams, tables) shadows; they use hairline borders and tonal fills.
